what_this_tests: Whether the COLLAPSE of covariate-shift OOD detection generalises outside dermatology. It does NOT test the inversion.

prediction_definitions.collapse: |mean Maha AUROC on B_heldout at lambda* - 0.5| <= 0.5 * |mean Maha AUROC on B_heldout at lambda=0 - 0.5| (3-seed means)
prediction_definitions.inversion: at any dense lambda > 0, mean Maha AUROC on B_heldout lies on the opposite side of 0.5 from lambda=0, by at least 0.05

hospital_assignment.A_split: patch-level, stratified by slide x label, random_state 42: 64% train / 16% checkpoint-select / 20% ID test (WILDS id_val convention; ID test shares slides with train)
hospital_assignment.B_split: by slide, GroupShuffleSplit test_size 0.3 random_state 42: B_adv slides [0,2,3,4,6,7,9] (38124 patches), B_heldout slides [1,5,8] (21312 patches). B labels never enter the classification loss.
hospital_assignment.C: hospital 2, all 85054 patches, never in any loss

recipe.backbone: DenseNet-121 ImageNet, BatchNorm1d on 1024-d features; classifier and GRL both on the normalised features
recipe.batches: 16 A + 16 B_adv per step (domain-balanced, as derm 50/50 ISIC/PAD)
recipe.optimiser: AdamW wd 1e-4; encoder 1e-4, domain head 1e-4 x 30, classifier 1e-4 x 0.2
recipe.grl: coef = lambda * max(0.2, 2/(1+exp(-20 p^0.5)) - 1), p = training progress
recipe.adversary_scaling_change_vs_phase12_1b: lambda multiplies the reversed gradient into the encoder only; the domain head minimises unscaled CE. Encoder gradient is identical to lambda*CE with GRL; the change removes lambda from the head's effective learning rate. Reason: in Phase 12.1b lambda in {10..300} scaled the head gradient as well (head lr x30), and the head sat at a constant uniform output with zero gradient from epoch 1.
recipe.lambda_0: coef = 0: the head still trains (online domain decodability is logged) but sends no gradient to the encoder
recipe.checkpoint: best ID accuracy on A checkpoint-select split
recipe.logging: adversary CE, adversary accuracy, mean per-sample norm of the reversed gradient at the features, and GRL coef, in 200-step windows from step 0; per-epoch adversary CE/accuracy

gates.adversary_learned: minimum over 200-step windows of mean adversary CE < 0.60. At chance from the first window onward is a null experiment.
gates.leakage_moved: post-hoc binary site probe (logistic, A ID test vs B_heldout, 70/30, 3 seeds, <=10000 per side) balanced accuracy at lambda <= lambda=0 value - 0.10
gates.id_competence: tumour accuracy on A ID test > 0.85 at lambda=0 and at every lambda in the dense set (3-seed means)
gates.detector_headroom: at lambda=0, Mahalanobis AUROC on B_heldout outside [0.45, 0.55]

dense_rule.lambda_star: smallest coarse lambda > 0 at which adversary_learned AND leakage_moved both hold
dense_rule.dense_set: {0, lambda*/sqrt(3) (3 significant digits), lambda*, next coarse lambda above lambda* if any}
dense_rule.reuse: seed-42 coarse runs are reused where the lambda coincides

stopping_rule: If ANY gate fails (adversary, leakage movement, ID competence, detector headroom), report the negative and stop. No third design, no escalation to a fourth dataset.
detectors: Mahalanobis class-conditional shared cov + 1e-3 I, cosine, kNN k=50 (30k stratified bank), MSP, Energy; statistics fit on A train only. ID reference = A ID test.
report_columns: leakage, ID balanced acc, ID ECE, OOD ECE (B_heldout), five detectors on B_heldout, hospital C Mahalanobis AUROC; per-epoch adversary logs; gate-by-gate pass/fail table
